source.title: Circuit Condensation: Post-Training that Concentrates a Behavior's Causal Circuit

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method—post-training with pruning and healing—to find and causally test a smaller IOI circuit, including interventions based on the published GPT-2 IOI role map.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a GPT-2 small IOI condensed circuit and causal role interventions. It also reports aggregate IOI circuit-removal results across models. Results on agreement, induction, docstring, and other model families do not establish that the original GPT-2 IOI head classes or roles generalize, so they are not included as claim-version rows. The text discusses alternative ablation conventions, but gives no IOI result under those alternatives.
record.test_reason: The study's main object is a LoRA-adapted ('condensed') GPT-2, which is not the claim's system. Two of its results do bear on the original model. First, interchange interventions under Wang et al.'s IOI algorithm are also run on the unmodified GPT-2 small (Table 16). Second, a frozen EAP-IG circuit selected at matched accuracy on the original model is compared with the 26-head role map (Table 19, App. H). These are a different method aimed at the same question, so T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The 24-head, 17-named circuit is in the adapted (LoRA) model and is described as a sufficient subcircuit, not a reconstruction of the published mechanism. The authors also report that frozen discovery on the original model needs 61 heads, 36 without documented roles. Their main conclusion is broader: condensation yields circuits 8.1× smaller than frozen baselines in 30 of 32 settings, making exhaustive verification feasible.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a LoRA adapter while iteratively pruning and healing edges, then tests the resulting adapted circuit. The original study analyzed the frozen GPT-2 small model and its 26-head IOI circuit. This is a post-training condensation study, not a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that mean and zero ablation can substantially change accuracy, but reports its circuit-size comparisons using interchange ablation. It does not give an IOI result under an alternative ablation convention. The reported IOI intervention results are aggregate across prompt pairs rather than separated by ABBA/BABA order.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA post-training with prune-and-heal reduces GPT-2 IOI to 24 heads (58 edges), 17 with published roles. The condensed circuit omits 9 of the 26 mapped heads, including 3 of 8 backup name movers and the previous-token stage. It keeps KL 0.056 to the original, and its retained heads cannot be swapped for same-layer heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training can concentrate IOI into a sufficient subset of the published GPT-2 circuit that still tracks the original model's outputs.

record.problems: The condensed circuit is trained and therefore is not the original frozen-model circuit. The GPT-2 IOI circuit does not reconstruct all mapped heads, and the role interventions cover selected roles only. Prompt-order results are not disaggregated; alternative ablation conventions are discussed but not tested for IOI in reported results.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted results on agreement, induction, docstring, and non-GPT-2 models because they do not test the specific GPT-2 small IOI head classes and roles in these claim versions. The paper’s IOI results under other ablation conventions are not reported, so none are entered as rows.

untested.parts: Faithfulness, completeness and minimality of the original 26-head circuit are not re-evaluated. Only the name-mover output and subject-inhibition variables are intervened on in the unmodified model.
Backup name-mover takeover after ablating the primary name movers is not tested. The paper only notes that C1 drops 3 of 8 backup heads.
No test of whether the same head classes and roles appear in other models, sizes or checkpoints, or are reused for other tasks.
No IOI result for the original circuit under mean or zero ablation, other metrics or other prompt distributions. The mean-ablation examples in App. K are for docstring only.
No breakdown by name order or template, and no more-name formats.

missing.what: Frozen EAP-IG circuit on unmodified GPT-2 small at matched accuracy: 61 heads (range 61–82), 25 of 26 named heads, 36 unnamed, precision 0.41, recall 0.96, F1 0.57, 256 edges, KL to original 0.50
Unmodified-model interchange intervention values as their own rows: output 0.995, subject-inhibition 0.645 (0.640–0.650), random 0.01, sham 0.01; frozen matched circuit 0.985 / 0.735 / 0.04 / 0.01

record.verdict_notes: Most of the record's rows concern the adapted model, a different system from the claim's GPT-2 small, so they are moved to none / fits_no_version. Only the unmodified-model intervention columns and the frozen matched circuit bear on the claim, and both are on the original model. V5 and V6 labels from the record are dropped. The aggregate removal result is not about evaluation sensitivity, and the combined accuracy has no per-format breakdown.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a trained, condensed GPT-2 small IOI circuit and selected role interventions, not whether the unmodified model’s full 26-head, 7-class circuit satisfies the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. It does not test every class or role.
The paper notes that it removes three of eight Backup Name Movers, but does not test whether backup heads take over when the primary Name Movers are ablated.

It evaluates condensed circuits across models and tasks, but does not test whether the same IOI head classes and roles carry the behavior across models or checkpoints, or whether those components are reused for other tasks.

The paper compares circuit sizes from discovery methods but does not test whether other methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same IOI circuit. It reports no IOI result under mean or zero ablation.
It reports a condensed circuit’s coverage of published roles and several IOI evaluations, but does not provide a GPT-2 IOI comparison across ablation conventions or prompt distributions.

IOI prompts include ABBA and BABA orders and corrupted prompts with a third name, but results are not broken down by order or template. Other templates, more-name formats, and separate mechanism comparisons are not tested.
